previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old female was admitted after transfer from a psychiatric facility due to altered mental status and lethargy. She had been heavily medicated, leading to toxic encephalopathy. Initial evaluation showed mydriasis and confusion, but imaging and labs were unremarkable. Medication polypharmacy was identified as the cause, and her regimen was simplified to lamotrigine and clonazepam. Her mental clarity improved significantly. She experienced a migraine during admission, treated with Fiorinal, and transient diarrhea that resolved spontaneously. MRSA and C. difficile screens were negative. She was medically cleared and discharged to extended psychiatric care with a streamlined medication plan, including lamotrigine, clonazepam, verapamil, and as-needed analgesics. Her mood and cognition stabilized, and she demonstrated insight into her condition.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with lap appendectomy two weeks ago, fever,
abdominal pain, tachycardia, right lower quadrant tenderness.  Question stump
appendicitis, abscess.

COMPARISONS:  CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial imaging is obtained following the administration of
intravenous and oral contrast material.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were
completed.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  The visualized heart and pericardium are
unremarkable.  There is no pericardial effusion.  The lung bases are clear. 
There is minimal atelectasis.  The liver enhances homogenously without any
focal lesions or intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The portal vein
is patent.  The gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands are
unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically without
any focal lesions or hydronephrosis.  No bowel obstruction.  Within the right
lower quadrant surgical bed ,there is a 2.3 x 2.4 x 5.2 cm rim-enhancing fluid
collection with surrounding stranding adjacent to the surgical clips
concerning for abscess and less likely postoperative seroma.  There is no free
air or lymphadenopathy within the abdomen.

CT PELVIS:  The bladder, rectum and sigmoid colon is unremarkable.  There is
an IUD in place within the uterus.  The adnexa are unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid, free air, or lymphadenopathy within the pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  There are no concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions.

IMPRESSION:  Rim-enhancing fluid collection with surrounding stranding in the
post-surgical bed in the right lower quadrant, highly concerning for abscess
and less likely postoperative seroma.

INDICATION:  ___ woman status post lap appendectomy two weeks ago, now
with right lower quadrant abscess, necessitating drainage.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___, abdominal imaging fellow and Dr. ___,
___ radiologist.

PROCEDURE:  The procedures, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed
with the patient and written informed consent was obtained.  A preprocedure
timeout was performed discussing the planned procedure, confirming the
patient's identity with three unique patient identifiers and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.

Preprocedure CT scan was obtained demonstrates mild bibasilar subsegmental
atelectasis.  A prominent heart size is noted.  Limited evaluation of the
solid organs without IV contrast.  Grossly normal upper abdominal solid organs
are noted.  Vicarious excretion of contrast is noted.  Residual contrast is
noted within the visualized colon.  Surgical clips are noted within the right
lower quadrant, with redemonstration of a rounded fluid collection within the
right paracolic gutter region.

Under CT fluoroscopy guidance, an entrance site was selected and the skin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  1% lidocaine was instilled
for local anesthetic.

A 15 ___ needle was advanced into the abscess under CT guidance.  Once
adequate positioning was confirmed, a wire was placed in collection to break
up loculations.  There was initial limited amount of material aspirated.  A
total of 10 cc of reddish/serosanguineous type fluid was aspirated with
internal tiny tissue debris noted.  Further attempt was made to aspirate
additional fluid without success.  Post-aspiration images demonstrated no
significant residual fluid collection and was thought the remaining finding
within the appendectomy bed likely represented solid tissue.

Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of Versed and
fentanyl throughout a total intraservice time of about 25 minutes, during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored by
radiology nursing personal.

The 10 cc of aspirated fluid was sent for microbiology.

The patient tolerated the procedure well with no immediate complication.

Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present throughout the entire
procedure.

IMPRESSION:

Successful CT-guided right lower quadrant abscess aspiration/drainage. 
Microbiology is pending.
